clue.text: Carol filled up with bitter when setting off

indicators.note: the carol word is stuffed full of the bitter word, so one sits inside the other

parts.note: to carol is to sing
tart means sharp or bitter in taste

explanation.surface: A carol singer's mood soured as they set out on their rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' reads as a person's name, but here it is the verb, to sing a carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe the moment of beginning a journey or process.

clue.text: Position for a good man, an engineer

parts.note: St, saint, is a good man
CE is a civil engineer

explanation.surface: A job for a virtuous man, an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good man' is the usual crossword ST for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A posture, or an attitude taken up on an issue.

clue.text: Present oneself as a very quiet listener

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet
an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Turning up as a hushed audience.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is the music marking pianissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up or come into view.

clue.text: Put under switch referred to

indicators.note: switch means the letters change places

explanation.surface: Placed beneath a switch that was mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' rearranges PUT UNDER; it reads as a light switch.
explanation.definitionFit: To look up a word in a book of reference is to consult it.

clue.text: Mark wants school back-up

indicators.note: in a down clue back-up means the school word is read upwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil needs support from the school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' turns ETON round, reading up the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A note can be a sign or mark, as in a note of distinction.

clue.text: Knock rubbish over and get the bird

parts.note: a rap is a knock

indicators.note: over signals the rubbish word is flipped round

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone bangs at a door, talks nonsense and is shown the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROT into TOR. 'get the bird' sounds like being booed off, but 'bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey such as a hawk or eagle is called by this name.

clue.text: It's all about a ring

parts.note: a round is a circle or ring

explanation.surface: A ring is what it is all about.
explanation.definitionFit: Everywhere on all sides, surrounding.

clue.text: Caterers involved in domestic rows

indicators.note: involved means the caterers' letters are tangled up

explanation.surface: Catering staff caught up in household quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges CATERERS. 'rows' are lines of houses, not arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of joined houses are rows of homes.

clue.text: Inhabitant having a party in the break

indicators.note: in places the party word inside the break word

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break
a side is a party in a dispute

explanation.surface: A local who throws a party during the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' means a tear, RENT; 'party' is a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in a place.

clue.text: A letter written by a priest, a non-conformist

indicators.note: a nonconformist refuses the usual order, so these letters break from their arrangement

explanation.surface: A dissenting clergyman pens a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-conformist' rearranges A PRIEST A. The 'letter' is not correspondence but the alphabet's H, the breathed sound.
explanation.definitionFit: In phonetics the letter H stands for a breathed sound, and the letter itself is so called.

clue.text: Goes on the stage

explanation.surface: An actor heads out to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: One embarks on a ship or bus; the theatre is known by its floor planks.

clue.text: Many substitute a strong colour

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many
an agent acts as a substitute for someone

explanation.surface: Many people swap in a bold shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid purplish red dye.

clue.text: Talk about the Continental style of building

indicators.note: about means the talk word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a chat is a talk
le is the French for the, French being a Continental language

explanation.surface: Chatting about European architecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Continental' is the French article, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss mountain cottage with wide eaves, a recognised type of house.

clue.text: Denied assistance, gets ahead

indicators.note: ahead tells us the gets word goes in front of the assistance word

parts.note: gains means gets or obtains
aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: Refused help, yet still gets in front.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints assistance first; 'ahead' moves the gets word to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or refuse is an old word for to deny.

clue.text: Indicate there's some wine to finish off

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
to end is to finish off

explanation.surface: Suggesting there's some wine left to polish off.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or signal what is coming.

clue.text: Do utter freely as instructed!

indicators.note: freely tells us the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to speak freely, as one has been told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges DO UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taught privately has been coached or instructed.

clue.text: Miserly in the home-and surly

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Miserly in the home-and surly (4)' for MEAN: 'in the home' gives no part of MEAN and looks like an OCR garble of a third definition; no scan to check.

clue.text: With little money about, cuts down orders

parts.note: p, a penny, is a small coin
re means about
pares means trims or cuts down

explanation.surface: Short of cash, someone trims their orders.
explanation.definitionFit: To get things ready and in order, arranging them.

clue.text: Firm leader

parts.note: reads like a strong, decisive leader, but is the person on the board running a company

explanation.surface: A strong-minded chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A board member managing a company heads the firm.

clue.text: Credit with having the very best

parts.note: owning means having

explanation.surface: Praised for possessing the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme, topping off everything, as in crowning glory.

clue.text: Managed without a single fall

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the managed word encloses the other

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a shop
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: Someone coped alone, never once stumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, so RAN goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Precipitation falls from the sky as water drops.

clue.text: The sculptor's figure is about right for size

indicators.note: about means the sculpture word goes round the other letter

parts.note: a statue is a carved figure made by a sculptor

explanation.surface: The sculpted figure is roughly the correct dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps STATUE round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Height or bodily build, and by extension standing, is measured in this word.

clue.text: A woman's article on pollution's read up

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue read up means the word runs upwards, backwards

parts.note: dirt is pollution, and the 's is an S

explanation.surface: A woman's essay about pollution has been studied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read up' reverses the pollution piece, giving STRID. 'A woman's' is the definition: a woman's name, with the 's acting as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian female first name.

clue.text: Scholar parking a vehicle in the street

indicators.note: in puts a vehicle inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An academic leaves a van on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person, especially an expert in a field.

clue.text: Port is for the large and lean

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for large
to tend is to incline or lean towards

explanation.surface: A harbour suited to fat and thin people alike.
explanation.walkthrough: OSTEND is a Belgian ferry port. 'lean' looks like thin but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian seaport on the North Sea.

clue.text: Polite requests made by a worker

parts.note: pleas are requests or appeals
a worker is a classic crossword term for an ant, the worker ant

explanation.surface: Courteous appeals made by a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' in crosswords is very often an ant or bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreeable and courteous in manner, a near synonym.

clue.text: Promises sport in an ocean-going vessel

indicators.note: in places the sport word inside the vessel letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
to sport a garment is to wear it

explanation.surface: Pledges of games aboard a liner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sport' looks like games but means to wear, as in sporting a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To vow or pledge solemnly is to take an oath.

clue.text: Hand out timber

explanation.surface: Distribute wood.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute cards; also pine or fir planks.

clue.text: An official statement concerning volte-face

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a volte-face is a turn about-face

explanation.surface: A formal announcement about a complete U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: A tax return is the official statement meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal report, such as a tax or election declaration, is filed under this name.

clue.text: Note some policemen retire in time to apply

indicators.note: in tells us the note and police letters go inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time
E is a musical note

indicators.note: retire means the police letters draw back, read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: Note that some officers stand down in time to put in an application.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' turns CID round to DIC. CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, is the British plain-clothes police branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote oneself to a task is to give it one's effort wholly.

clue.text: The skinhead tried to change step

indicators.note: head means the first letter of skin
to change means the following word is rearranged

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth attempted a new step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinhead' splits into 'skin' and 'head': its first letter S. 'to change' rearranges TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pace or step in walking.

clue.text: A quarter lit up, but that can be disregarded

parts.note: S, south, is one quarter of the compass
lighted means lit up

explanation.surface: Part of the town is illuminated, though nobody notices.
explanation.walkthrough: S for a compass point is a crossword convention for quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated with disdain or ignored, a slight being a snub.
